requirements.requirement: On node1, create a 512 MiB swap file and activate it immediately.
requirements.summary: The executor created /swapfile with an exact size of 536,870,912 bytes, root ownership, and mode 0600; initialized it as swap; and directly observed 512 MiB of active swap.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the swap file is automatically activated after future boots.
requirements.summary: A valid /etc/fstab entry was installed. A bounded reboot changed the boot identity, and post-restart checks directly showed the same swap file, persistent entry, active swap, and recovered OpenRC services.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. Node1 has an exact 512 MiB, securely permissioned swap file that was active immediately and automatically recovered after a demonstrated reboot. The mandatory restart protocol is complete and coherent: it includes healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, observed downtime, a changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered services and persistent swap state. Only a minor temporary-log residue affects hygiene.
limitations: The generic lifecycle failed-services probe was unsupported because the node uses Alpine/OpenRC rather than systemd; relevant OpenRC services were nevertheless checked directly before and after restart.
The fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot did not independently inventory swap or /etc/fstab, so those final-state conclusions rely on the direct executor post-restart command evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations were causally related to creating, activating, persisting, or reboot-testing the swap file. Temporary write tests were removed. The sole unnecessary retained residue was /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log, created by the reboot command and still present after execution; this is a minor, low-risk hygiene defect. Package health remained unchanged, and no unexplained service or security degradation was observed.
